$comment: Generated by maitento/app/SdkModelGenerator from the resource classes the .mtr compiler fills. Do not edit: run `dotnet run --project maitento/app/SdkModelGenerator`. Absent keys take their default (false / none).

values.description: Text in double quotes, taken exactly as written: `\n` stays a backslash and an `n`, and the text may run over several lines. Put anything long in a prompt file and use `@prompt("name")`.
A block of properties in braces, one `name = value` after another, with no commas.
A list in square brackets with commas between the items. A list cannot be empty: leave the property out instead.

references.description: Another definition, by name, in the namespace you deploy to. It may be declared in the same project, or already exist.
A definition by its id, without quotes.

includes.description: The text of a prompt file, as the value of a text property. It cannot be an item of a list.
The text of a JSON file, as the value of a text property, usually a JSON Schema. It cannot be an item of a list.

mapEntry.description: A map property takes one line per entry: the property's name, a colon and the key, then the value as text.

promptTemplate.description: In an interaction's task, and in the prompt files it includes, `%%name%%` is replaced by the run's input `name`. `{{#if name}}...{{/if}}` keeps its text only when the input has a value, and `{{#unless name}}...{{/unless}}` only when it has none. Every block must be closed.

resourceNames.description: A resource's name is its file name without `.mtr` (an app's is its folder's name). Use letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.` (but not `..`), at most 128 characters. Two files of the same kind may not have the same name, even in different sub-folders or with different capitals.

rules.text: Put spaces around `=`. Without them, the name, the `=` and the value read as one word.
A name with dots is one name. `inputs.prompts` is written as it is, never as a block named `inputs`.
A block holds `name = value` entries with no commas between them. Lists have commas.
A list cannot be empty. Leave the property out instead.
Numbers and `true` / `false` have no quotes, and text always has them.
Set each property once in a file, and once in each block.
`@prompt` and `@json` give the value of a text property. They cannot be items of a list.
A file needs at least one property or comment: an empty file does not build.
rules.right: // Settings for this app: none yet.

kinds.title: Agent
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the agent's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: An agent: a model with standing instructions, a one-line summary and the tools it may use. An agent does nothing on its own; an interaction puts it to work.

properties.name: model
properties.description: The AI model the agent runs on, by its catalogue name: `@ref("provider.model")`.

properties.name: prompt
properties.description: The agent's standing instructions (its system prompt): who it is and how it behaves. Use `@prompt("name")` for anything longer than a sentence. Run inputs (`%%name%%`) are not filled in here; they belong in the interaction's `task`.

properties.name: summary
properties.description: One line that describes the agent to other agents: a router choosing who answers, or a manager choosing who to hand work to, reads it.

properties.name: functions
properties.description: The tools the agent may call in every interaction it takes part in.

properties.name: routedSubAgents
properties.description: Makes the agent a router. On every turn it is given, its model picks one of these agents (by their `summary`, guided by this agent's `prompt`) and that agent takes the turn instead. The first one is the fallback.

properties.name: allowSwarm
properties.description: Lets the agent start other interactions as sub-runs, where the interaction it takes part in allows them (its `swarm` block).

properties.name: allowWebSearch
properties.description: Gives the agent the built-in web search tool.

properties.name: allowWebFetch
properties.description: Gives the agent the built-in web fetch tools, which read any URL as text.

kinds.title: One-shot interaction
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the one-shot interaction's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: A one-shot interaction: one agent, one task, one answer.

properties.name: agent
properties.description: The seat: the name the agent goes by here, and which agent fills it.

properties.name: task
properties.description: What the agents are asked to do. The run's inputs are filled in where it says `%%name%%`, and `{{#if name}}...{{/if}}` keeps text only when an input has a value (`{{#unless name}}` for the opposite). Use `@prompt("name")` for anything longer than a sentence.

properties.name: functions.openApi
properties.description: Tools available to every agent in the interaction, as well as the tools each agent has itself.

properties.name: inputs.prompts
properties.description: The inputs a run is started with, which the `task` uses as `%%name%%`.

properties.name: inputs.functions.binding
properties.description: Run inputs whose values go straight into a tool call, such as a customer id: the model never sees or chooses them.

properties.name: inputs.functions.auth
properties.description: Run inputs that choose the secret a tool sends with its calls.

properties.name: schema.solution
properties.description: The JSON Schema the answer must match, usually `@json("name")`. The run's output is then JSON of that shape.

properties.name: prompts.system.mode

enum.description: They are added after Maitento's instructions.
They replace everything: the agent's prompt, Maitento's instructions and the list of tools.
They replace Maitento's general guidance, keeping the agent's prompt, safety rules and tools.

properties.description: How `prompts.system` combines with the instructions Maitento gives every agent.

properties.name: prompts.system
properties.description: Extra system instructions for every agent in the interaction.

properties.name: duration.warn
properties.description: When the agents are told that time is running short, as `"hh:mm:ss"` from the start of the run.

properties.name: duration.max
properties.description: The longest a run may take, as `"hh:mm:ss"`. The run stops with an error when it is reached. Time spent waiting for a person does not count. No limit when not set.

properties.name: context
properties.description: How the conversation is kept within the model's context window, and how many rounds of tool calls an agent may make in one turn. The defaults suit almost every interaction.

properties.name: loom
properties.description: Long-term memory for the interaction's agents. No memory when not set.

properties.name: credentialStack
properties.description: The credential stack this interaction's runs use, by name, when their start doesn't name one: its credentials serve every model call, and Maitento's own keys never do. Leave it out to use the namespace's default stack, then your tenant's.

properties.name: swarm
properties.description: Other interactions the agents may start as sub-runs, and how many. None when not set.

kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the managed interaction's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: A managed interaction: a manager agent owns the task and hands pieces of work to named team members, who see only what the manager sends them. The manager's final reply is the answer.

kinds.title: Connector
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the connector's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: A connector: one HTTP endpoint, described once. Its method and URL, its parameters, the shape of its request and response, and the kind of credential it needs. Agents never call a connector directly: a tool points at it.

properties.name: method
properties.description: The HTTP method.

properties.name: url
properties.description: The endpoint's full URL. `{name}` in it marks a path parameter, declared in `parameters.path`.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the endpoint does, in a sentence (500 characters at most).

properties.name: parameters.path
properties.description: The parameters in the URL's path, one for each `{name}` in `url`.

properties.name: parameters.query
properties.description: The query-string parameters.

properties.name: schema.request
properties.description: The JSON Schema of the request body, usually `@json("name")`. The model's arguments are checked against it before the call is made. Without one, no body is sent, even for a POST.

properties.name: schema.response
properties.description: The JSON Schema the endpoint's response must match, usually `@json("name")`.

properties.name: postProcessResponseUnicodeCharacters
properties.description: Replace typographic characters in the response (curly quotes, dashes, bullets, the ellipsis) with plain ones before it is read. Applies when `schema.response` is set.

properties.name: auth

enum.description: No credential is sent.
A secret's value, sent in an HTTP header that the tool names.
A short-lived Maitento token, for connectors that call Maitento's own API.

properties.description: The kind of credential the endpoint needs. The credential itself is given where a tool uses the connector.

kinds.title: Tool
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the tool's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: A tool: what an agent sees and calls. It points at a connector, tells the model when to use it, fixes any values the model must not choose, supplies the credential, and can require a person's approval.

properties.name: connector
properties.description: The connector the tool calls.

properties.name: bindings.path
properties.description: Fixed values for the connector's path parameters, one line each: `bindings.path:orderId = "A-1001"`.

properties.name: bindings.query
properties.description: Fixed values for the connector's query parameters, one line each: `bindings.query:units = "metric"`.

properties.name: bindings.request
properties.description: Fixed values for fields of the request body, which the model never sees or chooses, one line each: `bindings.request:field = "value"`. Separate the names of a nested field with `/` (`bindings.request:customer/id`). A value is read as the type the request schema gives the field.

properties.name: auth
properties.description: The credential sent with every call, from a secret. The connector needs `auth = "Header"`.

properties.name: guidance
properties.description: When and how to use the tool. The model reads it to decide when to call the tool and with what, so write it for the model. The connector's description when not set.

properties.name: requiresApproval
properties.description: A person must approve each call before it is made. The run waits with status `PendingApproval`. A tool that needs approval cannot be called from an app.

kinds.title: Capsule
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the capsule's name.
kinds.description: A capsule: the recipe for a short-lived Linux sandbox. Which packages to install, which users to create, which file systems and secrets to mount and which commands to run when it starts. It ends when its commands finish (with `autoTerminate`), when it is stopped, or when it runs out of time.

properties.name: template
properties.description: A base image name, recorded with the capsule. Every capsule runs on the same image today (with Python 3, Node.js 22, .NET 8 and .NET 10, Java 17, git and build tools), so it does not change what runs.

properties.name: packages
properties.description: Extra Debian packages to install with `apt` when the capsule starts, such as `["jq", "sqlite3"]`. Lowercase letters, digits, `+`, `-` and `.`; each named once.

properties.name: users
properties.description: Linux users to create. Commands run as the default user unless they say otherwise.

properties.name: vfs
properties.description: Virtual file systems to mount. Each one appears at `/mnt/<mountName>`.

properties.name: secrets
properties.description: Secrets to mount. Each one is written to the file `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`, readable by the default user.

properties.name: startup
properties.description: Commands to run, in order, when the capsule starts. Their output is not kept.

properties.name: autoTerminate
properties.description: Stop the capsule as soon as its startup commands have finished.

properties.name: maxDuration
properties.description: The longest the capsule may run, as `"hh:mm:ss"`, counted from when it starts. Ten minutes when it is not set. A capsule still starting up then fails; a ready one finishes, and the command it is running is stopped.

kinds.title: Loom
kinds.name: The file name without `.mtr` is the loom's name. Other files refer to it as `@ref("<name>")`.
kinds.description: A named loom: a long-term memory several interactions can share. A participant uses it with `loom = @ref("name")` on its seat. A deploy creates the loom, or brings its description and settings up to date; it never touches what the loom remembers, and removing the file does not delete the loom.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the loom is for, shown in the portal.

properties.name: nightWeaving
properties.description: Tidy up the loom once conversations go quiet: summarise them, merge duplicates, note contradictions and write a short portrait of each person.

properties.name: quietMinutes
properties.description: Minutes without activity before night weaving starts.

properties.name: weaverModel
properties.description: The catalogue model that night-weaves the loom, such as `"anthropic.haiku-4.5"`. The model of the agent whose conversation it is when not set.

kinds.title: App settings
kinds.name: Each sub-folder of `apps/` is one app, named after the folder; the `.mtr` file in it may have any name.
kinds.description: An app's settings: the optional `.mtr` file beside an app's Cogniscript (`.mtc`) code. The app's inputs come from the parameters of its `main` function, not from this file.

properties.name: functions.openApi
properties.description: Tools the app's code calls with `ExtOpInvoke`. Listing a tool here pins the version it had when the app was deployed; a tool that is not listed is called at its latest version.

properties.name: duration.max
properties.description: The longest a run of the app may take, as `"hh:mm:ss"`. The run is stopped when it is reached.

properties.name: credentialStack
properties.description: The credential stack the app's runs use, by name, when their start doesn't name one, and every interaction and code pipeline they start. Its credentials serve every model call, and Maitento's own keys never do. Leave it out to use the namespace's default stack, then your tenant's.

AgentExternalOperationReference.description: A tool the agent may call, wherever it takes part: `{ ref = @ref("current-weather") }`.

properties.name: ref
properties.description: The tool.

properties.name: guidance
properties.description: A note kept with the agent about how it should use the tool. The model reads the tool's own `guidance`; to change that for one interaction, set `guidance` where the interaction binds the tool.

AuthenticationHeader.description: A credential sent with every call of a tool: `auth = { header = "X-Api-Key" secret = @ref("orders-api-key") }`. The tool's connector needs `auth = "Header"`.

properties.name: header
properties.description: The HTTP header the secret's value is sent in. For `Authorization`, a value without a space is sent as `Bearer <value>`.

properties.name: secret
properties.description: The secret whose value is sent. Create the secret before you deploy.

CapsuleSecretMount.description: A secret written to a file in the capsule: `{ secret = @ref("deploy-key") mountName = "deploy-key" }`.

properties.name: secret
properties.description: The secret. Create it before you deploy.

properties.name: mountName
properties.description: The file name: the secret's value is written to `/mnt/secrets/<mountName>`.

CapsuleStartupCommand.description: A command the capsule runs when it starts: `{ command = "python3" arguments = ["report.py"] }`.

properties.name: command
properties.description: The program to run, such as `"python3"` or `"bash"`.

properties.name: arguments
properties.description: The program's arguments. Each is passed as one word exactly as given, so spaces and quotes inside an argument reach the program. To pipe or redirect, run `sh` with arguments `["-c", "<line>"]`.

properties.name: runAsUser
properties.description: The user to run the command as, one of the capsule's `users`. The default user when not set.

properties.name: maxDuration
properties.description: The longest the command may run, as `"hh:mm:ss"`. Five minutes when it is not set.

properties.name: wait
properties.description: Wait for the command to finish before the next one starts. Set `false` to start it and move on.

CapsuleUserDefinition.description: A Linux user the capsule creates: `{ name = "builder" sudoAs = ["deployer"] }`.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The user name: lowercase letters, digits, `_` and `-`, starting with a letter or `_`, at most 32 characters, and not `root`.

properties.name: sudoAs
properties.description: Other users of the capsule this user may run commands as, with `sudo`. Never `root`.

CapsuleVirtualFileSystemMount.description: A virtual file system mounted in the capsule: `{ vfs = @ref("sales-data") mountName = "data" }`.

properties.name: vfs
properties.description: The virtual file system. Create it before you deploy.

properties.name: mountName
properties.description: Where it appears: `/mnt/<mountName>`.

InteractionAgentBinding.description: A seat in an interaction: the name a participant goes by, and the agent that fills it. `{ name = "Greeter" agent = @ref("greeter") }`.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the participant goes by in this interaction. The other participants, and the transcript, use it, so give each seat its own.

properties.name: agent
properties.description: The agent that fills the seat.

properties.name: loom
properties.description: A named loom the participant always remembers with, instead of the one the interaction's `loom` settings would give it. A loom chosen when the run starts still takes precedence.

properties.name: webAccess
properties.description: The participant's built-in web tools, overriding what its agent allows: `webAccess = { search = true fetch = false }`. Leave either out to keep the agent's own setting. Where this block and `webAccess.search` / `webAccess.fetch` are both given, the block wins.

properties.name: webAccess.search
properties.description: Gives or takes away the built-in web search tool for this participant, overriding its agent.

properties.name: webAccess.fetch
properties.description: Gives or takes away the built-in web fetch tools for this participant, overriding its agent.

properties.name: functions.openApi
properties.description: Tools for this participant only, as well as the interaction's and its agent's own.

InteractionAgentWebAccess.description: A participant's built-in web tools: `webAccess = { search = true fetch = false }`. Leave either out to keep its agent's own setting.

properties.name: search
properties.description: Gives (`true`) or takes away (`false`) the web search tool.

properties.name: fetch
properties.description: Gives (`true`) or takes away (`false`) the web fetch tools.

InteractionConnectorAuthenticationSecret.description: A run input that chooses the secret a tool sends with its calls: a run gives the id of the secret, such as one per customer. `{ function = @ref("get-order") name = "customerKey" header = "X-Api-Key" }`.

properties.name: function
properties.description: The tool whose calls send the secret.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The input's name: a run gives the input's value under this name.

properties.name: agent
properties.description: Only the participant filled by this agent sends it. Every participant when not set.

properties.name: secret
properties.description: The secret sent when a run does not choose one.

properties.name: header
properties.description: The HTTP header the secret's value is sent in.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the input is for, shown to whoever starts a run.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Whether a run must give the input. A run without a required input is refused, unless the input has a default, which the run then uses.

InteractionConnectorBindingInput.description: A run input whose value is written straight into a tool's calls, so the model never sees or chooses it: `{ function = @ref("search-handbook") name = "partitionId" target = "partitionId" type = "request" }`.

properties.name: function
properties.description: The tool whose calls get the value.

properties.name: target
properties.description: Where the value goes: the name of the request body field (separate the names of a nested field with `/`), or of the path or query parameter, as `type` says.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The input's name: a run gives the input's value under this name.

properties.name: agent
properties.description: Only the participant filled by this agent gets the value. Every participant when not set.

properties.name: default
properties.description: The value used when a run does not give one.

properties.name: type

enum.description: A field of the request body.
A query-string parameter.
A path parameter.

properties.description: What `target` names: a field of the request body, a query parameter or a path parameter.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the input is for, shown to whoever starts a run.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Whether a run must give the input. A run without a required input is refused, unless the input has a default, which the run then uses.

InteractionContextSettings.description: `context = { ... }`: how an interaction keeps its conversation within the model's context window, and how many rounds of tool calls an agent may make in one turn. The defaults suit almost every interaction.

properties.name: mode

enum.description: Nothing until the conversation reaches the model's hard limit; then it is shortened just enough to be sent.
The conversation is shortened once it passes the target share of the window: large tool results first, then the oldest turns in the middle, with a notice that it was trimmed.
Accepted, and trims as Automatic does.
No trimming: a conversation that no longer fits makes the run fail, instead of going on without part of it.

properties.description: What happens when the conversation no longer fits the model's context window.

properties.name: targetUtilization
properties.description: How full the context window may get, as a fraction from 0 to 1, before the conversation is shortened.

properties.name: toolResultTrimming.mode

enum.description: Never: tool results are kept as they came back.
When the conversation no longer fits the context window.
Once an agent has had a set number of turns: every result but the latest.
Both: after a set number of turns, and whenever the conversation no longer fits.

properties.description: When the results of earlier tool calls are replaced, to save space.

properties.name: toolResultTrimming.maxCycles
properties.description: For `toolResultTrimming.mode = "AfterCycles"` or `"Both"`: once an agent has had this many turns, every tool result but the latest is replaced.

properties.name: toolResultTrimming.replacement
properties.default: [Tool result trimmed to reduce context size]
properties.description: The text a replaced tool result becomes, with `toolResultTrimming.style = "Placeholder"`.

properties.name: toolResultTrimming.style

enum.description: The same replacement text for every result.
A digest of what was there: which tool was called, with what, how large the result was, and how it began. Made without a model call, so it costs nothing.

properties.description: What a replaced tool result becomes.

properties.name: compaction.type

enum.description: The agent summarises its own conversation. Usually the best summary, since the agent already understands it, but an agent with strict instructions may refuse.
A separate call, without the agent's instructions, writes the summary, so one is always made. It loses the agent's own understanding.
No summaries: the conversation is only trimmed.

properties.description: Whether, and how, older parts of a long conversation are summarised to make room. Suits long, many-turn conversations such as chats.

properties.name: compaction.atUtilization
properties.description: How full the context window gets, as a fraction from 0 to 1, before the conversation is summarised.

properties.name: compaction.keepRecentTokens
properties.description: The most recent part of the conversation kept word for word when it is summarised, in tokens.

properties.name: compaction.targetTokens
properties.description: The length the summary aims for, in tokens.

properties.name: maxToolCallLoops
properties.description: The most rounds of tool calls an agent may make in one turn. After that its tools are withheld and it must answer. `0` means no limit.

properties.name: responseMaxTokens
properties.description: The most the model may write in one reply, in tokens, including any reasoning. `0` allows the model's maximum. A value above the model's maximum is lowered to it; a reply that reaches the limit is kept as far as it got.

properties.name: compaction.maxTokens
properties.description: The most a summary may be, in tokens. Used only with `compaction.type` set.

InteractionLoom.description: `loom = { ... }` on an interaction: long-term memory for its agents. A bare `loom = { enabled = true }` gives each agent a fresh memory for every run, with suggested recall and suggested weaving.

properties.name: enabled
properties.description: Turns memory on. `false` keeps the settings but leaves memory off.

properties.name: scope

enum.description: A fresh loom for every run. One caller's threads never reach another's run.
One loom per agent (or one for the interaction, when shared) that lasts across every run.
One loom per value of the run input named by the scope input, such as one per user.

properties.description: Whose memory a run uses, and so whether it lasts beyond one run.

properties.name: scopeInput
properties.description: For `scope = "Input"`: the run input whose value picks the memory, such as `"userName"`.

properties.name: shared
properties.description: All the interaction's agents share one memory. Otherwise each agent has its own.

properties.name: recall

enum.description: Nothing is offered: the agent searches its memory only when it chooses to.
The agent is told what may connect, and chooses whether to recall it.
The relevant threads are shown in the conversation straight away.

properties.description: How remembered threads come back into a conversation.

properties.name: weave

enum.description: Only the agent weaves, with its LoomWeave tool.
The weaver reads each exchange and offers what may be worth keeping; the agent decides.
The weaver weaves weak threads directly; use strengthens them, and disuse lets them fade.

properties.description: How new memories are made from a conversation.

properties.name: tapestryTokens
properties.description: How long the "what you know" summary an agent is given when a conversation starts may be, in tokens.

properties.name: subjectInputs
properties.description: Run inputs that name who the agents are working with, such as `"userName"`, so memories are about the right person.

properties.name: nightWeaving
properties.description: Tidy up the memories this interaction creates once a conversation goes quiet: summarise it, merge duplicates, note contradictions and write a short portrait of each person.

properties.name: quietMinutes
properties.description: Minutes without activity before night weaving starts.

properties.name: weaverModel
properties.description: The catalogue model that reads conversations to make memories and to night-weave, such as `"anthropic.haiku-4.5"`. The agent's own model when not set.

properties.name: vetModel
properties.description: A lightweight catalogue model, such as `"anthropic.haiku-4.5"`, that checks what memory offers an agent in the middle of a conversation and drops what does not belong. Off when not set.

properties.name: vetRecall
properties.description: The `vetModel` also checks what an agent's own searches of its memory bring back.

properties.name: seedFrom
properties.description: A named loom every memory this interaction creates starts from: a new person's memory starts knowing what the shared loom knows.

properties.name: readFrom
properties.description: Named looms the agents may read but never change.

InteractionPromptInput.description: An input a run is started with, used in the `task` as `%%name%%`: `{ name = "topic" description = "What the haiku is about" required = true }`.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The input's name: a run gives the input's value under this name.

properties.name: type

enum.description: Text.
A whole number.
A number that may have a fractional part.
true or false.

properties.description: The type of value the input takes.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the input is for, shown to whoever starts a run.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Whether a run must give the input. A run without a required input is refused, unless the input has a default, which the run then uses.

InteractionSwarm.description: `swarm = { interactions = [ @ref("country-facts") ] maxConcurrent = 5 }`: other interactions this one's agents may start as sub-runs, wait for and combine. An agent also needs `allowSwarm = true`.

properties.name: interactions
properties.description: The interactions that may be started. Nothing else can be. They may be declared in the same project, this one included.

properties.name: participants
properties.description: The seats (by `name`) that may start them. Every seat whose agent allows it when not set.

properties.name: maxDepth
properties.description: How many levels of sub-runs may be started below this one. 1 when not set; at most 4.

properties.name: maxConcurrent
properties.description: How many sub-runs may run at once, across the whole tree. 5 when not set; at most 20.

properties.name: maxTotal
properties.description: How many sub-runs may be started in all, across the whole tree. 20 when not set; at most 100.

ManagedInteractionAgentBinding.description: A team member the manager can hand work to, and what it sees when it is asked: `{ name = "Writer" agent = @ref("writer") mode = "Private" }`.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the participant goes by in this interaction. The other participants, and the transcript, use it, so give each seat its own.

properties.name: agent
properties.description: The agent that fills the seat.

properties.name: mode

enum.description: A fresh start every dispatch: its own persona and the manager's message, nothing more. Kept for audit, never shown again.
A conversation of its own with the manager, kept across dispatches: every message the manager sent it and every reply.
The shared conversation: the manager's own words, the human's, and every dispatch to a group agent with its reply, like a round-robin where it speaks only when the manager hands it the turn.

properties.description: What the team member sees when the manager hands it work.

properties.name: loom
properties.description: A named loom the participant always remembers with, instead of the one the interaction's `loom` settings would give it. A loom chosen when the run starts still takes precedence.

properties.name: webAccess
properties.description: The participant's built-in web tools, overriding what its agent allows: `webAccess = { search = true fetch = false }`. Leave either out to keep the agent's own setting. Where this block and `webAccess.search` / `webAccess.fetch` are both given, the block wins.

properties.name: webAccess.search
properties.description: Gives or takes away the built-in web search tool for this participant, overriding its agent.

properties.name: webAccess.fetch
properties.description: Gives or takes away the built-in web fetch tools for this participant, overriding its agent.

properties.name: functions.openApi
properties.description: Tools for this participant only, as well as the interaction's and its agent's own.

OpenApiExternalOperationBinding.description: A tool made available in one place (to a whole interaction, to one participant, or to an app), with any values and credentials that apply there: `{ ref = @ref("search-handbook") }`. What is set here overrides the tool's own settings.

properties.name: ref
properties.description: The tool.

properties.name: bindings.path
properties.description: Fixed values for the connector's path parameters, one line each: `bindings.path:orderId = "A-1001"`.

properties.name: bindings.query
properties.description: Fixed values for the connector's query parameters, one line each: `bindings.query:units = "metric"`.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The name the model calls the tool by here. The tool's own name when not set.

properties.name: bindings.request
properties.description: Fixed values for fields of the request body, which the model never sees or chooses, one line each: `bindings.request:field = "value"`. Separate the names of a nested field with `/` (`bindings.request:customer/id`). A value is read as the type the request schema gives the field.

properties.name: auth
properties.description: A credential to send with every call made here, instead of the tool's own.

properties.name: guidance
properties.description: When and how to use the tool here, instead of the tool's own `guidance`. The model reads it.

properties.name: terminal
properties.description: A successful call ends the agent's turn: the result is recorded, and the model is not asked to continue. Use it for a "finish" tool that is meant to be the last thing an agent does in a turn.

OpenApiParameter.description: A path or query parameter of a connector: `{ name = "latitude" description = "Latitude in decimal degrees" type = "number" }`.

properties.name: description
properties.description: What the parameter means. The model reads it to choose a value.

properties.name: name
properties.description: The parameter's name, as the endpoint expects it. A path parameter's matches `{name}` in the URL.

properties.name: type

enum.description: Text.
A number that may have a fractional part.
A whole number.
true or false.

properties.description: The type of value the model must give.

properties.name: required
properties.description: Whether a call must give the parameter.

RoundRobinInteractionFeatures.description: `features = { ... }`: which moves the agents at the table may make.

properties.name: noAction
properties.description: An agent may pass its turn without saying anything.

properties.name: voting
properties.description: Agents vote on a proposed answer.

properties.name: directQuestions
properties.description: An agent may ask another a question directly.

properties.name: solutionProposal
properties.description: An agent may propose a final answer. With no one able to, a conversation with a person carries on until it is stopped.

RoundRobinInteractionHumanInLoopSettings.description: `human = { first = true }`: a person takes part in the conversation.

properties.name: first
properties.description: The person speaks first. Otherwise the agents speak first and the person last.

properties.name: votes
properties.description: Round-robin only: the person votes too, when an agent puts something to a vote. Needs `features.voting`.

properties.name: solutions
properties.description: Round-robin only: a proposed final answer is put to the person too, to accept or reject. Needs `features.solutionProposal`.

RoundRobinInteractionRules.description: `rules = { ... }`: when a round-robin conversation ends on its own.

properties.name: noActionLoops.max
properties.description: How many rounds in which every agent passes end the run. No limit when not set.

aiModel.title: AI model
aiModel.description: An AI model from the model catalogue, by its catalogue name (`provider.model`).
aiModel.source: The model catalogue: `@ref("provider.model")`, such as `@ref("deepseek.deepseek-v4-flash")`. List the names with `mt aimodel-list` or the API.

secret.title: secret
secret.source: Secrets are not part of a project: create them in the portal, with the SDK or with `mt secret-create` before you deploy.

virtualFileSystem.title: virtual file system
virtualFileSystem.source: Virtual file systems are not part of a project: create them in the portal, with the SDK or with `mt vfs-create` before you deploy.

files.title: Prompt file
files.description: Text for any text property, included with `@prompt("name")`: `prompts/name.md`, in any sub-folder of `prompts/`. A file is found by its name alone, so keep names unique. The text may use the run's inputs as `%%name%%`, and `{{#if name}}...{{/if}}` / `{{#unless name}}...{{/unless}}` blocks, which must be balanced.

files.title: JSON file
files.description: JSON, usually a JSON Schema, included with `@json("name")`: `json/name.json`, in any sub-folder of `json/`. A file is found by its name alone, so keep names unique.

files.title: App code
files.description: An app's program, in Cogniscript: `apps/<app>/*.mtc`, at least one per app (an app folder without one is skipped). The program starts at `main`, and `main`'s parameters are the app's inputs. An optional `.mtr` beside it holds the app's settings.

includes.description: Replaced by the prompt file's text when the code is compiled, so it goes where a value goes: `string task = @prompt("name");`. Inside a text value it is plain text. A missing file fails the build.
Replaced by the JSON file's text when the code is compiled, as text: `jsonObject schema = StringToJsonObject(@json("name"));`. Inside a text value it is plain text. A missing file fails the build.

files.title: Code pipeline definition
files.description: A code pipeline: `code-pipelines/<pipeline>/pipeline-definition.json`. Its `name` must be the folder's name. A pipeline folder without the file is skipped.

includes.description: Replaced by the text of the pipeline's own prompt file, as a JSON string. A missing file fails the whole build.
Replaced by the text of the pipeline's schema file, as a JSON string. A missing file fails the whole build.
Replaced by the id of a tool, which may be declared in the same project.

files.title: Code pipeline hook
files.description: Cogniscript functions a code pipeline runs between its phases: `code-pipeline-hooks/<pipeline>/*.mtc`. Every function in the folder is a hook, helpers included, so each one takes exactly two parameters: `(string processId, string methodName)`. Maitento writes the folder's `main` when you deploy, so a `main` of your own fails the deploy.

includes.description: Replaced by the prompt file's text when the code is compiled, so it goes where a value goes: `string task = @prompt("name");`. Inside a text value it is plain text. A missing file fails the build.
Replaced by the JSON file's text when the code is compiled, as text: `jsonObject schema = StringToJsonObject(@json("name"));`. Inside a text value it is plain text. A missing file fails the build.

Replaced by the prompt file's text, escaped to sit inside a JSON string inside a text value. `mt`, the SDKs and the portal replace it wherever it appears in the file, comments included, before the code is compiled.
Replaced by the schema file's text, escaped and replaced in the same way as `@promptJson`.
